title: Style the host with a theme value
summary: The :host selector styles the custom element itself.
introduction: The :host selector styles the custom element itself. Your task: Change --note-colour and check the component text.
learningObjectives: Change --note-colour and check the component text.
Explain the example for style the host with a theme value

blocks.text: The :host selector styles the custom element itself. A CSS custom property can pass a theme choice into a shadow tree.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<style>themed-note { --note-colour: navy; }</style><themed-note></themed-note>
<script>
  class ThemedNote extends HTMLElement {
    constructor() { super(); this.attachShadow({mode:"open"}).innerHTML = "<style>:host { display:block; color:var(--note-colour, green); padding:1rem; }</style>Read a story today."; }
  }
  customElements.define("themed-note", ThemedNote);
</script>
blocks.title: Style the host with a theme value

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`attachShadow` creates the component's internal shadow root. Open mode allows access through its `shadowRoot` property.
`:host` styles the custom element that owns the shadow root, rather than an ordinary inner child.

blocks.text: The custom element has padding and navy text. If the custom property is missing, it uses green.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use documented theme properties to customise a component. Avoid depending on the names of private internal elements.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change --note-colour and check the component text.
